author: human
request:
Feature request: filter the vet list by specialty. Three product decisions
come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of
  scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in.
  Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The JSON endpoint at /vets is reinstated as a supported surface — this
  filter is its first requested capability. Mint a fresh requirement for it;
  the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused.
- The filter is a URL contract only. Neither surface gains a form, dropdown,
  or other page control in this request; pagination links carry the
  parameter so filtered pages stay navigable. A visible control may come as
  a follow-up request.

Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` query parameter:

- /vets.html?specialty=<name> — the HTML page shows only vets holding that
  specialty; pagination applies to the filtered list.
- /vets?specialty=<name> — the JSON endpoint returns only those vets.

Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive — not a prefix. A
specialty matching no vet yields the normal page or JSON document with an
empty vet list (HTTP 200). An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if
the parameter were absent, like the empty owner search. Without the parameter
both endpoints behave as today. Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Reader can filter both veterinarian lists by specialty through the URL
summary: The directory page and the reinstated JSON list accept an optional specialty parameter and show only the veterinarians holding that specialty, matching the whole name regardless of letter case. Pagination applies to the filtered list, and its links keep the filter.
acceptance_criteria: Given no specialty parameter, when either list is requested, then every veterinarian is returned as before the filter existed.
Given a specialty name, when /vets.html is requested with it, then the page shows only the veterinarians holding that specialty.
Given a specialty name, when /vets is requested with it, then the JSON document lists only the veterinarians holding that specialty.
Given a name differing from a specialty only by letter case, when either list is requested with it, then that specialty matches on every supported database.
Given the beginning of a specialty name, when either list is requested with it, then that specialty does not match.
Given a name matching no veterinarian's specialty, when either list is requested with it, then the reader gets HTTP 200 and the normal page or document with an empty list.
Given an empty or whitespace-only value, when either list is requested with it, then the result is the same as with no parameter.
Given more matching veterinarians than fit one page, when the filtered page is opened, then it shows one page of the matches and counts pages from the matches alone.
Given a filtered page with more than one page of matches, when a pagination link is followed, then the next page stays filtered.
Edge case 2: a veterinarian holding the named specialty and others is listed with all of their specialties.
Edge case 3: a veterinarian matching the filter appears exactly once across the filtered pages.
Edge case 4: a value with spaces around a specialty name is matched as given, so it matches no specialty.
Edge case 5: a value containing characters reserved in a URL reaches the next page intact through the pagination links.
non_goals: NG-9 stands narrowed: free-text veterinarian search, pet search, and visit search stay out.
NG-10: no form, dropdown, or other page control on either surface.
Filtering by any attribute other than specialty, or by several specialties in one request.
Paging the JSON list, or changing how an out-of-range page number is handled.
New user-facing wording, including any no-match message on the page.
Reusing REQ-VET-002, which stays withdrawn.
notes: Requirement mapping: REQ-VET-003 is the fresh requirement the owner asked for. It covers the JSON list as a supported surface and the filter on both lists, so the slice stays one behavior under the intake's req_id. Narrowest readings taken, recorded under PRD Open Questions: surrounding spaces on a non-blank value are not ignored (edge case 4); a repeated specialty parameter stays undefined; a veterinarian's name is not filtered. Autofix audit: no prd-autofix records. Outside this agent's write scope, for system-design-expert: docs/system-design.md still calls the JSON route requirement-less and pending removal, and says no JSON API exists for primary workflows; the Vets row carries no requirement; docs/adr/README.md needs an index row for the 2026-10-30 non-goal ADR.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The specialty filter fits the vet feature package: VetController binds and normalizes the parameter, VetRepository owns the match, and there is no service layer (system-design.md Overview, Contracts). New ground: the first cross-vendor case-folded query and the first caller-keyed read beside the vets cache, each recorded in an ADR. Blank-to-absent is request-shape binding under the Web controller row of architecture-principles.md § Pattern Catalog, tested at web level per testing-principles.md § Seams. The whole-name match is a query predicate, never controller logic. Reinstating /vets contradicts nothing current: the owner decision and PRD retire the Known Defects row, and the server-side rendering ADR still holds because no JSON API backs the primary workflows. No foundational signal trips. Oracle basis: IDE not connected, so symbols were confirmed by grep and direct source reads, the weaker basis.
integration_points: Binding, /vets.html and /vets: a request-scoped optional String parameter named specialty on each handler; no persisted type is bound, so no allow-list applies. isBlank decides absent; any other value reaches the repository unstripped (edge case 4). Unlike owner search, never strip.
Absent parameter: both handlers call the existing cached findAll methods unchanged.

Repository: two new read-only methods, one Pageable returning Page<Vet>, one returning the whole collection, sharing one @Query JPQL: EXISTS over v.specialties with lower(s.name) = lower(:specialty), ORDER BY v.id. @Param binding. No @Cacheable. The membership test avoids duplicates from a join and leaves count and all specialties correct.

Template: the filter value reaches all six pagination hrefs through Thymeleaf link parameters, @{/vets.html(page=...,specialty=...)}, replacing the __${}__ preprocessed strings. With no filter the hrefs stay exactly as today, with no empty specialty parameter; verify how a null link parameter renders. No visible control and no new message key (NG-10).
Double, framework transport: MockMvc in VetControllerTests (the sanctioned mock).

Double, repository at the web seam: the existing @MockitoBean VetRepository in VetControllerTests, stubbed on the exact argument and never any(), so the outcome shows which value was sent. Reason: the class already runs as a @WebMvcTest slice with this double, and a hand-written Spring Data double would re-implement the query the repository tests prove. Web-level tests here: no parameter, blank values, unchanged value with surrounding spaces, both surfaces' filtered output and empty list, links keeping the filter, reserved characters.

Double, repository at the query seam: none. New VetRepositoryTests uses @DataJpaTest with @AutoConfigureTestDatabase(replace = NONE), as ClinicServiceTests does, on real H2. It owns letter case, prefix, spaces, all specialties held, appears-once, and page counting, with extra rows through TestEntityManager because the seed holds only six veterinarians. Place each prd-entry test_name at the seam that proves it.
Double, vendor seam: none. PostgresIntegrationTests and MySqlIntegrationTests each gain one case-differing filter read on the real database; they skip without Docker.

patterns.description: @Transactional(readOnly = true) on each read; keep it, omit @Cacheable on the new reads

risks.risk: Filter on the vet list path: a cached filtered read keyed by caller text grows the unbounded vets cache (system-design.md § Scale and Load, Specialty-filter reads row).
risks.mitigation: Parameterized membership-test query with no cache annotation, per the vet cache ADR; a bounded path otherwise, so simplest readable form.

risks.risk: Letter-case match passes on H2 and fails elsewhere (system-design.md § Persistence; PRD criterion on every supported database). Owner search on PostgreSQL is the recorded precedent.
risks.mitigation: Fold both operands in JPQL per the case-folding ADR; the PostgreSQL and MySQL integration tests exercise it.

risks.risk: Unsorted paging can repeat or skip a veterinarian across pages (system-design.md § Persistence; PRD edge case 3).
risks.mitigation: ORDER BY v.id in the filtered query; leave the unfiltered read as it is.

risks.risk: A raw value concatenated into a link breaks on reserved characters and is an injection pattern (security-principles.md § Language Realization, Cross-site scripting; system-design.md § Threat Model; PRD edge case 5).
risks.mitigation: Encoded Thymeleaf link parameters only. Test values containing & + # % and a space against the rendered href.

risks.risk: NUL in the value (%00) is rejected by the PostgreSQL driver, turning a no-match into an error page against the HTTP 200 criterion (security-principles.md § Trust Boundaries, External input; architecture-principles.md Web controller row).
risks.mitigation: Treat a value containing NUL as matching nothing at the controller's binding step: empty page or document, no query. Tested at web level.

risks.risk: On a MySQL database built by user.sql, the pad-space utf8_general_ci collation matches a trailing-space value, against edge case 4 (system-design.md § Persistence). Accents are ignored there too. The Compose database is no-pad on trailing spaces.
risks.mitigation: Accepted for this slice and recorded in Persistence; no vendor-specific predicate. Surfaced to the owner in notes.

risks.risk: Malformed page values on the filtered route (architecture-principles.md Web controller row; prd-entry non_goals).
risks.mitigation: Out of scope: out-of-range page handling stays unchanged.

notes: Design writes: Overview, Contracts rows (Vet, Specialty, Vets, VetRepository, VetController), Persistence, new § Scale and Load built from the doctor template (the section was absent), Security Context, Threat Model; Known Defects row for the machine-readable route removed; ADR index gains the non-goal ADR and two new ADRs. A repeated specialty parameter stays undefined per the PRD Open Questions; Spring joins it with a comma, so it matches nothing. Owner item: the user.sql MySQL trailing-space behaviour is a vendor-collation gap the PRD does not settle. Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records.

recommendations: Conjectural, not reproduced: on a MySQL database built by src/main/resources/db/mysql/user.sql (user.sql:4 `DEFAULT CHARACTER SET utf8`), a value holding a 4-byte character such as an emoji may raise an illegal-mix-of-collations error against the utf8mb3 column at VetRepository.java:70, turning a no-match into HTTP 500. approved_aspects: Injection into data access: the one new input reaches the database only as a bound parameter. VetRepository.java:70 reads `WHERE EXISTS (SELECT s FROM v.specialties s WHERE lower(s.name) = lower(:specialty))` and :73 binds `@Param("specialty") String specialty`. author: product-requirements-expert
title: Reader can filter the veterinarian directory page by specialty through the URL
summary: The directory page at /vets.html accepts the optional specialty parameter and shows only the veterinarians holding that specialty, a page at a time. Pagination counts the matches alone, and its links keep the filter. This completes REQ-VET-003, after the JSON list slice.
acceptance_criteria: Given a specialty name, when /vets.html is requested with it, then the page shows only the veterinarians holding that specialty.

Given a name differing from a specialty only by letter case, when /vets.html is requested with it, then that specialty matches on every supported database, including a stored name that holds capitals.
Given the beginning of a specialty name, when /vets.html is requested with it, then that specialty does not match.
Given a name matching no veterinarian's specialty, when /vets.html is requested with it, then the reader gets HTTP 200 and the normal page with an empty list.
Given a value containing a NUL character, when /vets.html is requested with it, then the reader gets HTTP 200 and the normal page with an empty list.
Given an empty or whitespace-only value, when /vets.html is requested with it, then the result is the same as with no parameter.
Given more matching veterinarians than fit one page, when the filtered page is opened, then it shows one page of the matches and counts pages from the matches alone.
Given a filtered page with more than one page of matches, when a pagination link is followed, then the next page stays filtered.
Given no specialty parameter or a blank value, when the directory has more than one page, then its pagination links carry no specialty.
Edge cases 2 and 3: a veterinarian holding the named specialty and others appears exactly once across the filtered pages, with all of their specialties.
Edge case 4: on the page, a value with spaces around a specialty name is matched as given, so it matches no specialty.
Edge case 5: a value containing characters reserved in a URL reaches the next page intact through the pagination links.
non_goals: NG-9 stands narrowed: free-text veterinarian search, pet search, and visit search stay out.
NG-10: no form, dropdown, or other page control on either surface.
Filtering by any attribute other than specialty, or by several specialties in one request.
Paging the JSON list, or changing how an out-of-range page number is handled.
New user-facing wording, including any no-match message on the page.
Changing the JSON list's filter behavior delivered by the previous slice.
Reusing REQ-VET-002, which stays withdrawn.

The stored-capitals row must fail if lower(s.name) is removed. The pagination name persists more holders than one page and asserts the page content, total elements, and total pages. The across-pages name walks every page and asserts one appearance of a holder of several specialties, with all of them (edge cases 2 and 3).
